extracted.intended_audience: U.S. patent applicants/appellants, patent practitioners, and patent examiners (USPTO practice)
extracted.subtask_description: Procedural rules and substantive requirements governing replies, petitions, reopening prosecution, substitute examiner's answers, fees, and oral hearing practice in U.S. patent appeals (MPEP §§1207-1209).

rubrics_metrics.name: Petition to seek review of undesignated new ground (37 CFR 1.181) — timing
rubrics_metrics.description: Any request to seek review of the primary examiner’s failure to designate a rejection as a new ground of rejection must be by petition to the Director under 37 CFR 1.181 filed within two months from the entry of the examiner’s answer and before the filing of any reply brief.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Failure to timely file such a petition constitutes a waiver of any arguments that a rejection must be designated as a new ground of rejection. If a petition is granted, a two-month period to file a reply under 37 CFR 1.111 to reopen prosecution is provided; if refused, a two-month period to file a single reply brief under 37 CFR 41.41 is provided. Any reply filed within two months but before decision on petition will be treated as withdrawal of the petition and maintenance of the appeal.

rubrics_metrics.name: Options when examiner's answer contains a new ground of rejection (37 CFR 41.39(b))
rubrics_metrics.description: If an examiner’s answer contains a rejection designated as a new ground of rejection, appellant must within two months either (1) reopen prosecution by filing a reply under 37 CFR 1.111 (with or without amendment/affidavits/evidence relevant to the new ground), or (2) maintain the appeal by filing a reply brief under 37 CFR 41.41 addressing each new ground of rejection.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A request to reopen prosecution under (1) will be entered and treated as a request to withdraw the appeal. A reply brief under (2) must follow the brief requirements (37 CFR 41.37(c)) and may not be accompanied by amendments/affidavits/evidence; if accompanied, it will be treated as a request to reopen prosecution. The two-month period is the controlling timing (see extension rules).

rubrics_metrics.name: Requirements for a reply that reopens prosecution (37 CFR 1.111 compliance)
rubrics_metrics.description: A reply filed to reopen prosecution must address each new ground of rejection set forth in the examiner’s answer in compliance with 37 CFR 1.111 within two months of mailing of the examiner’s answer. The reply may include amendments, evidence, and/or arguments directed to claims not subject to the new ground.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Any amendment/affidavit/evidence included must be relevant to the new ground. If the reply is not fully responsive but is bona fide, the examiner should provide a time period to complete the reply pursuant to 37 CFR 1.135(c). If the reply is not bona fide and the two-month period has expired, the examiner must sua sponte dismiss the appeal as to the claims subject to the new ground. Upon a compliant reply, the examiner must reopen prosecution and consider the reply; the examiner may make the next Office action final unless a newly-introduced ground is improper (not necessitated by amendment or not based on permitted IDS information). See MPEP § 706.07(a).

rubrics_metrics.name: Requirements and limits of filing a reply brief to maintain the appeal (37 CFR 41.41 & 41.37 compliance)
rubrics_metrics.description: To maintain the appeal in response to a new ground of rejection, appellant must file a reply brief within two months that addresses each new ground of rejection in compliance with 37 CFR 41.37(c)(1)(iv) and 37 CFR 41.41. The reply brief should include an identification page and argument pages, each starting on a separate page.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A reply brief may not include any new or non-admitted amendment, affidavit, or other evidence; if accompanied by such materials, it is treated as a request to reopen prosecution. Any argument raised in the reply brief which was not raised in the appeal brief, or is not responsive to an argument in the examiner’s answer, will not be considered by the Board unless good cause is shown. Jurisdiction passes to the Board on filing the reply brief (or upon expiration of the period). The examiner normally will not answer a reply brief unless the Board remands.

rubrics_metrics.name: Consequences of failing to timely reply to a new ground or substitute answer
rubrics_metrics.description: If appellant fails to timely file a reply under 37 CFR 1.111 or a reply brief in response to an examiner’s answer (or substitute examiner’s answer) that contains a new ground of rejection, the appeal will be sua sponte dismissed as to the claims subject to that new ground; if all claims are affected, the entire appeal is dismissed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Where only some claims are subject to the new ground, dismissal of the appeal as to those claims authorizes cancellation of those claims and the appeal continues as to remaining claims. After dismissal, the examiner should follow the MPEP procedures (e.g., § 1215).

rubrics_metrics.name: Reopening prosecution after appeal by examiner (SPE approval and considerations)
rubrics_metrics.description: An examiner may, with approval from the Supervisory Patent Examiner (SPE), reopen prosecution to enter a new ground of rejection in response to appellant’s brief. In deciding whether to reopen prosecution or add a new ground, examiners and supervisors should consider the degree to which the rejection previously of record is being changed, any previous reopenings after the appeal brief, and overall pendency of the application.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Office action containing a new ground may be made final if (A) necessitated by amendment, or (B) based on information presented in an IDS under 37 CFR 1.97(c) where no 1.97(e) statement was filed. Ordinarily after-final amendments/affidavits/evidence not previously entered must be entered and considered on the merits; where multiple conflicting after-final amendments are filed, the first amendment should be entered and subsequent conflicting amendments should not be entered. Use form paragraph 12.239 when reopening prosecution after appeal. SPE approval/signature is required.

rubrics_metrics.name: Form paragraph 12.239 (reopening prosecution) — content and effect
rubrics_metrics.description: Form paragraph 12.239 may be used when reopening prosecution and informs that 'PROSECUTION IS HEREBY REOPENED' and sets out options appellant must exercise to avoid abandonment (file reply under 1.111/1.113 or initiate a new appeal via notice of appeal and new brief). It notes fee application and requires SPE approval.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Form lays out practical consequences: appellant must act to avoid abandonment; previously paid appeal fees may be applied to a later appeal (with possible fee differences if fees increased); detailed bracket instructions for insertion of dates/reasons and SPE signature. Use of the form ensures appellant is notified of next steps and avoids unintended abandonment.

rubrics_metrics.name: Substitute examiner’s answer responding to a remand — appellant options and requirements (37 CFR 41.50)
rubrics_metrics.description: If the Board remands for further consideration of a rejection and a substitute examiner’s answer is provided, appellant must within two months either (i) reopen prosecution by filing a reply under 37 CFR 1.111 with or without amendment/affidavit/evidence relevant to the remand issues, or (ii) maintain the appeal by filing a reply brief per 37 CFR 41.41. Any new ground in a substitute examiner’s answer must comply with MPEP § 1207.03.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A substitute examiner’s answer may only be furnished in response to a remand. Amendments/affidavits/evidence must be relevant to issues in the remand. If appellant does not timely respond, appeal will be sua sponte dismissed as to the remanded claims. A Technology Center Director or designee must approve substitute examiner’s answers (form ¶12.285 and signature).

rubrics_metrics.name: Remands for matters other than further consideration of rejection — reply brief only (no reopening option)
rubrics_metrics.description: When the Board remands an application for reasons not for further consideration of a rejection (e.g., to consider an information disclosure statement filed while Board had jurisdiction, or to consider an amendment or affidavit), the examiner may provide a substitute examiner’s answer and appellant may respond by filing a reply brief within two months; appellant does not have the option to request reopening under 37 CFR 41.50(a) unless the remand was for further consideration of a rejection.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Consideration of any IDS or petition filed while the Board possessed jurisdiction will be held in abeyance until the Board’s jurisdiction ends. The reply brief deadline and content rules (no new amendments/evidence) apply as appropriate.

rubrics_metrics.name: Two-month time periods and extensions — non-extendability under 1.136(a) and permitted extensions
rubrics_metrics.description: The two-month time periods (for filing petitions, replies to examiner’s answers/substitute answers, reply briefs, payment of forwarding fee, or requesting oral hearing) are not extendable under 37 CFR 1.136(a), but may be extendable under 37 CFR 1.136(b) for patent applications and 37 CFR 1.550(c) for ex parte reexamination proceedings.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Extensions under 1.136(a) are not allowed for these two-month periods; practitioners must use 1.136(b) (fee-based extensions) or the appropriate reexamination rule. The rule is reiterated across sections (41.39(c), 41.40(e), 41.50(a), 41.41(c)).

rubrics_metrics.name: Reply brief — single reply rule and timing (37 CFR 41.41(a))
rubrics_metrics.description: Appellant may file only a single reply brief to an examiner’s answer within the later of two months from the examiner’s answer or a decision refusing a petition under 37 CFR 1.181.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This single-reply rule is explicit; extensions are limited as noted above. Normally filing a reply brief is not required and if none is filed the application is forwarded to the Board; filing is required in response to certain situations (e.g., designated new grounds or substitute answers remanding for further consideration).

rubrics_metrics.name: Restrictions on content of reply briefs (no new/non-admitted amendments/evidence)
rubrics_metrics.description: A reply brief shall not include any new or non-admitted amendment, or any new or non-admitted affidavit or other evidence. Any new amendment must be submitted in papers separate from the reply brief; a paper containing an amendment is not a reply brief and will not be entitled to entry simply because it is labeled 'reply brief.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: New or non-admitted affidavits or other evidence are not permitted in a reply brief. Entry of separate amendment papers is governed by 37 CFR 41.33 (and related rules for after-final papers). Arguments in reply briefs that were not previously raised in the appeal brief, or are not responsive to the examiner’s answer, will generally not be considered by the Board absent good cause.

rubrics_metrics.name: Fee for forwarding an appeal to the Board (37 CFR 41.45) — timing and consequences
rubrics_metrics.description: Appellant must pay the appeal forwarding fee set forth in 37 CFR 41.20(b)(4) within the later of two months from the date of either the examiner’s answer or a decision refusing a petition under 37 CFR 1.181 to designate a new ground of rejection. Failure to pay within the period results in dismissal of the appeal.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The examiner's answer should notify the appellant of the forwarding-fee requirement (form paragraphs 12.279/12.279.01). The forwarding fee requirement was added effective March 19, 2013; the earlier appeal brief fee was reduced to $0 and the forwarding fee was added. The forwarding-fee requirement is waived where the appeal brief fee was paid before March 19, 2013. The forwarding fee does not apply to inter partes reexamination appeals.

rubrics_metrics.name: Oral hearing — when to request, procedural requirements, and limits (37 CFR 41.47)
rubrics_metrics.description: An oral hearing should be requested only when appellant considers it necessary or desirable; to request an oral hearing appellant must file a separate paper captioned 'REQUEST FOR ORAL HEARING' with the fee within two months from the examiner’s answer or on the date of filing a reply brief, whichever is earlier.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If no timely request/fee is filed, appeal will be decided on the briefs. If granted, a hearing date is set; oral argument ordinarily limited to 20 minutes for appellant and 15 minutes for examiner unless otherwise ordered. Appellant may rely only on evidence previously entered and arguments relied upon in the brief/reply brief, except that upon a showing of good cause new argument based on a recent relevant Board or Federal Court decision may be allowed. The Board may also decide a hearing is not necessary even if requested.
